To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

prostate cancer stem cell survival and growth are regulated by androgen and estrogen receptor signaling, and that new drugs targeting these receptors are promising in the treatment of prostate cancer.
prostate cancer stem/progenitor-like cells express classical and novel estrogen receptors and are, therefore, resistant to androgens and to androgen deprivation treatment.
prostate cancer stem cell survival is mediated by estrogen receptors, and that the use of new anti-estrogen compounds may lead to significant advances against prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel targets in androgen-independent prostate cancer, with the goal of improving the therapeutic management of this disease.
understanding the role of androgens and estrogens in prostate cancer, with the aim of developing novel and effective therapies for this disease.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of prostate cancer stem cells, and we believe that the identification of new molecular targets will lead to new therapeutic options.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prostate cancer stem cell plasticity, which is a hallmark of this disease, is a major challenge to the development of novel and effective therapeutic approaches.

the androgen and estrogen receptor systems play a pivotal role in prostate cancer initiation, progression, and resistance to androgen deprivation treatment, and thus, they represent promising targets for prostate cancer treatment.
prostate cancer stemness and the development of castration-resistant prostate cancers are the result of the interplay between the androgen and estrogen receptor pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prostate cancer stem cell is a promising target for the development of novel drugs in prostate cancer.

androgen receptor antagonism is the most promising approach to treat prostate cancer, but the use of anti-estrogen compounds, alone or in combination with antiandrogens, may also represent a valuable strategy.
androgen deprivation therapy is still the first-line treatment for prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the androgen and estrogen receptor pathways are not only critical to normal prostate development and homeostasis but also play a major role in prostate cancer initiation, progression, and resistance to treatment.
the development of new drugs targeting androgen and estrogen receptor signaling may be a promising approach to overcome the resistance of prostate cancer stem cells to androgen deprivation therapies.
the development of new drugs that specifically target androgen and/or estrogen receptors may lead to a better management of prostate cancer, including castration-resistant forms.
